title: Linear-Probing Hash Table
prompt:
Fixed-capacity int→int table with linear probing and tombstones:
 
```c
#define HT_CAP 16
typedef struct { int key; int val; unsigned char state; } ht_ent_t; /* state: 0 empty, 1 used, 2 tombstone */
void ht_init(ht_ent_t *t);
int ht_put(ht_ent_t *t, int key, int val); /* 1 stored, 0 full */
int *ht_get(ht_ent_t *t, int key);   /* pointer to val, or NULL */
int ht_del(ht_ent_t *t, int key);   /* 1 deleted, 0 absent */
```
 
Hash: `((unsigned)key * 2654435761u) % HT_CAP`. Probe forward with wraparound; insert may reuse tombstones; the table is never resized.

tests.name: insert and find
tests.hint: Hash lands somewhere; probe finds it; get returns a pointer to live storage.

tests.name: collision probes forward
tests.hint: Both keys hash to the same slot; the second probes forward, and both remain findable.

tests.name: tombstone reused
tests.hint: Deleting the home slot leaves a tombstone; the new colliding key reuses it; the removed key is gone.

tests.name: full table
tests.hint: 16 distinct keys fill the table; the 17th reports full.
